about: Findings in NexaForge SecureCode itself. A finding is closed only while its check passes on the shipped code; if the check fails again it is regressed.

findings.what: A scanner binary planted in the scanned repo ran on Windows and could fake a clean scan
git could write into the agent's own settings (redirect, --work-tree)
Force-push, public repo, path normalisation, UNC, escaped secret names, Monitor tool and MCP path keys bypasses
Non-object tool input failed open
Console output injection, null scanner JSON crash, symlinked files followed
Per-edit hook scanned the whole working folder when the file was outside it and timed out
Storage redirect hop followed further redirects, including to http
Release zip took every file in the folder, including local drafts
Writes into the agent's config folder through programs outside the write-verb list (curl -o, tar, mkdir, npm --prefix, .NET file APIs) and redirect forms
git clone/init/diff --output/archive, GIT_DIR env, -C home into the config folder; option abbreviations and aliases for force push and hard reset
Trailing dot, AppData/../.., spaces in user name, \\?\UNC, cd tracking, links and subst
Directory junctions were followed
Quadratic path collapsing on long input
Semgrep injection rules rated WARNING never blocked at --fail-on high
Headers check passed if any file mentioned a header name
A signer file saved with a byte order mark made every update fail
No changed files were found in a repo with no commits; git resolved from the project folder
An organization's internal product name left in public files
Psalm (which loads project code) ran without --run-tests
Backtracking regex on packagist names (ReDoS)
Test-path downgrade and cookie skip depended on folders above the project
A malformed Retire.js or Psalm report crashed the gate
Metadata host with a trailing dot, 169.254.x.x.nip.io, instance-data and api-prod hosts accepted
Uncommitted edits could ship and an empty index signed an empty zip
Recorded task name passed to schtasks unvalidated; task XML decoded as UTF-8 only
A Notepad BOM in update.json broke install and update

Writes into the agent's config folder or the runtime through macOS /Users, root-relative \Users, ~user, $env:SystemDrive, Documents and Settings, %USERPROFILE:~0%, wildcards (.cl*, OrgAIS*), tree copies or extraction into the home folder, and readers that run code or write (ForEach-Object, Where-Object, sort -o, uniq, method calls)
Secret reads through wildcards (~/.ssh/id*, ~/.aws/cred*, ~/.git-cred*, *env) and unknown names (.envrc, gcloud application_default_credentials.json)

In ci mode the scanned repo could silence scanners (.gitleaks.toml allowlist, .gitleaksignore, # nosemgrep, .semgrepignore, .trivyignore, trivy.yaml). ci mode now uses package-owned settings; a repo .gitleaksignore (which gitleaks 8.x always reads) is itself a HIGH finding
Force, delete or mirror push through -c remote.x.push=+ref, git config remote.x.push/mirror, git remote add --mirror, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n env and git send-pack --force
Download piped into perl, py, $SHELL, exec sh, b\ash, xargs bash, timeout zsh; perl -e "$(curl)", backticks; [scriptblock]::Create((irm URL))
gh gist create --public/-p, GraphQL visibility with spaces, gh api --input to repo, gist or GraphQL endpoints
Startup-file persistence through cp, sed -i, Copy-Item $PROFILE and the zsh, fish and other login files the list did not name
MCP arguments named url or href (browser_navigate file:///.../.env) were not checked; file: URLs are now percent-decoded

IDOR through route model binding is not found by the static rules (benchmark L18); the skill's authz matrix and cross-user tests are the control. Fixed: laravel-idor-route-model-binding reports a bound model with no policy, gate, can() or owner guard, and the gate drops it when routes/*.php (->can(), can:, admin role, scopeBindings() with a checked parent) or a FormRequest authorize() covers it. Not modelled: checks in helper methods or one branch only, run-time policies, global scopes, Route::bind(), middleware in bootstrap/app.php or Kernel.php, ->except() in controller middleware
findings.check: py -I benchmark/run_lab.py --mode full --lab laravel (L18 found, 0 of 4 clean files reported); tests/test_benchmark_lab.py::test_laravel_lab_full_floor; tests/test_laravel_authz.py::test_gate_route_context and ::test_gate_realistic_app_has_no_findings_left

findings.what: Scanners installed by securecode setup live in a user-writable folder the agent guard does not protect yet; a program or prompt-injected agent writing there could swap a scanner for a fake
findings.check: tests/test_guard_positive_model.py::test_scanner_tools_folder_writes_are_denied_reads_allowed and ::test_nexaforge_tools_dir_override_is_protected (closed by V7G-05 in the guard merge)

findings.what: Only the engine's own wheel or npm package is hash-checked; their dependencies are resolved by pip or npm and are not pinned by hash

The pattern holds a literal backspace character where \b was meant, so its v-html branch never matches (VUE_RAW_HTML still reports v-html). Found during the 7.0 engines work; not changed there to avoid duplicate findings
Assignment regex was quadratic per line (a$a$a$...): 42 s on an 800 KB file
Line numbers counted from offset 0 per method: 69 s on a 2.9 MB controller, and no cap on findings
Throttle/auth group stack rescanned per route: 62 s on a 2 MB routes file
CRITICAL on template words (required, System, include) next to $_GET; argument lists reported as CRITICAL
Uploads/ and Images/ with capitals and <?= in images were missed
IDENTIFIED BY / PASSWORD '...' values, quoted passwords with spaces, salts and base64 blobs were echoed in findings
A junction or symlink named app/ was followed outside the project and could lower a severity

permitAll on /env and /console missed; FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING treated as XXE fix; principal null check treated as owner check; FPs on @jakarta.validation.Valid, RestTemplate.execute, SHA-256 of reset tokens, shuffleMappings
LOAD DATA LOCAL reported as DB_GRANT_ALL; now DB_LOCAL_INFILE
Unquoted code expressions (X_SECRET = re.compile(...)) read as short secrets; found by the self-scan

Suppression expiry was compared as a string and Python 3.11+ fromisoformat accepts 20260115 and 2026-W01, so such entries never expired. Only YYYY-MM-DD is accepted now; anything else counts as expired with a NOTE naming the entry

findings.where: scripts/secgate.py collect_semgrep, collect_trivy, collect_gitleaks, collect_retire, collect_psalm, main
findings.what: Malformed scanner JSON (wrong types, deep nesting, huge numbers) crashed the gate with AttributeError or RecursionError. It is now a NOTE 'scanner output unreadable' and the required scanner counts as failed (ci mode blocks)
Literal BOM, bidi and zero-width characters in tracked source; replaced with escapes and guarded by a repo-wide test

nuclei accepted [fd00:ec2:0::254], [::ffff:100.100.100.200], metadata.goog and decimal, octal and hex IPv4 forms of metadata and private addresses; the ZAP wrapper had no host checks and ran bare 'docker'. Both now use scripts/dast_target.py (browser-style parsing, resolve once, metadata and link-local always refused, private and loopback only when named in SECURITY_DAST_PRIVATE_HOSTS) and docker comes from an absolute PATH lookup
False positive on setParameter("n", "%" + note + "%"), a bound parameter; concatenation inside binding-call arguments is no longer SQL_CONCAT. Spring lab clean files reported: 0 of 1
nuclei resolves the staging host again itself, so a DNS answer that changes between the check and the scan can still move a nuclei scan (ZAP is pinned with --add-host). The URL is set by a person

Found in self-review before commit: the owner-mode approval text showed only the collapse() form, which reads ./x/../../y as y, so the person could approve a different path than the one that runs. The literal command is now shown first, with the collapsed form added only when it differs

Design hazard for owner mode, fixed before it shipped: a class result (destructive, exposure) returning early would skip the later deny checks, so a force push redirected into ~/.claude or a hard reset inside ~/.claude would only ask. Every deny rule now runs on the statement and the protected-write check in git_rule comes before the class checks
Found in self-review: publish and install were judged only at the pipeline head, so sh -c 'npm publish', timeout 60 npm publish or cmd /c npm publish were not classed

Relative paths reached ~/.claude from a project under home (../../.claude, cd ~/Documents && cp x ../.claude, git -C ../.., tar -C ../.., gci ..\.. -Recurse | Remove-Item, links and junctions to ..\..): the tracked folder was unused and follow_cd dropped it

Shell syntax was not modelled: brace expansion, [^x] classes, backslash-newline inside words, $'\x2e' quoting, process substitution, escaped option letters (find -ex\ec, sort -\o, sort --out), functions and aliases shadowing readers, writing a script and running it in the same command
Python startup persistence: .pth in the interpreter prefix or site dirs and sitecustomize packages were allowed through Bash and Write
Quadratic regex on long runs of slashes (20k slashes took 18 to 24 s, near the 20 s hook timeout)
Secret reads through ~/.ssh/i*, ~/.ssh/./*, ~/.s?h/*, ~/.aws/c*, brace and [^x] forms, whole-folder reads (grep -r . ~/.ssh, tar -c ~/.ssh | base64, gci ~/.ssh | gc) and line continuation inside .env
Home spellings $env:TEMP\..\..\.., $env:APPDATA\X\..\..\.., $env:HOMEPATH, $PWD\..\.., [Environment]::GetFolderPath were not resolved; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR was not protected

Tools skipped the guard: the hook matcher was an allowlist (Artifact and other tools never reached it) and MCP write detection keyed on tool-name verbs (browser_take_screenshot filename, save_file, keys to and content_path)
Download-and-run shapes: | python3.12, | nodejs, | awk system, c\url ... | sh, httpie http, base64 -d | sh, powershell /enc and en-dash -enc
The stop gate (and scanners that run git) honoured the repo's .git/config, so core.fsmonitor, hooks, filter and textconv drivers could run code; .git/config writes were allowed
The stop gate skipped non-ASCII and quoted file names (git core.quotePath)
False positives seen live: a quoted grep pattern with \| split the command and the lone backslash read as the root; a python heredoc naming ~/Downloads/x.pdf was denied as the home folder itself
The 7.0 scanner tools folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\NexaForgeTools, ~/.local/share/nexaforge-tools, NEXAFORGE_TOOLS_DIR) could be written by the agent, which could swap a scanner for one that always passes

Cursor's generic preToolUse hook is not wired to the guard yet, so file writes by the Cursor agent (including to its own hooks.json) are not checked. Re-checked on 2026-11-03: cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks lists preToolUse with Write and Delete matchers, but documents neither their tool_input fields nor whether the hook runs before the edit is applied, so it stays open until a live Cursor test confirms both

Only shell commands are classed: an MCP tool that publishes a package or creates a public repo, gh repo sync --force, and wrappers with their own arguments (sudo -u x npm publish) are not recognized as exposure or destructive
findings.check: SECURITY-CONTEXT.md (Owner mode vs managed mode, known gaps)

findings.what: Code execution inside allowed commands is out of scope: a project script or test the agent wrote in an earlier tool call can itself write outside the project (python build.py, npm test). The guard only sees command text. Use Claude Code's native sandbox where available.
findings.check: SECURITY-CONTEXT.md (positive model, what is out of scope)

findings.what: diff.external and per-driver diff commands from the repo's config cannot be switched off through the environment (an empty value makes git fail); the stop gate passes --no-ext-diff and git log only uses them with --ext-diff, but a scanner that ran plain git diff would honour them
findings.check: tests/test_safe_git.py (no scanner in the gate runs git diff today)

findings.what: The daily task was created with schtasks /TR, which has a 261-character limit: a long Python or app path (a venv under a deep folder) made the installer skip the update task with only a 'skipped' line, and test_brand_overlay failed for that reason on a longer venv path. The task is now created from an XML definition (XML-escaped paths, no /TR limit) by the System32 schtasks.exe

A machine that was off or asleep at 11:00 skipped that day's update check (schtasks /SC DAILY without catch-up; cron on Linux and macOS). Windows now has StartWhenAvailable, a logon trigger, a network condition, a one-hour limit and restart on failure; --update-timer installs a Persistent systemd user timer or a RunAtLoad launchd agent

A GitHub rate limit (403 or 429) was reported as a failure and retried on every run; a download cut short was only caught as 'signature invalid'. Rate limits are now a logged back-off with a bounded retry time, and a size different from the release listing or Content-Length is 'download-incomplete'

Task Scheduler restarts a task only when it fails to start, not when updater.py exits with an error, and the systemd service has no Restart= (Type=oneshot with Restart= fails to load on systemd before 244). After a network error the next try is the logon trigger, the next boot or the next day, not 30 minutes later

Found in the independent review of the 7.0 merge: only the first 200 filter, diff and merge driver keys were neutralised, so a repo with 200 dummy drivers and one real one ran its program through the stop gate and the scanners; a config git could not list was read as empty. Too many drivers or an unreadable config now refuses to run git at all

Found in the independent review: log.showSignature with gpg.ssh.program (or the x509 and openpgp verifiers) in the repo's config ran a repo program on git log -p, which gitleaks runs. These keys are now switched off

Found in the independent review: an update started by the launchd agent runs the new installer, whose launchctl bootout of the same job would kill the update half way. A loaded agent is now left alone
findings.check: tests/test_update_mechanism.py::test_macos_update_never_boots_out_the_running_agent (code path only; not run on a real Mac)

findings.what: Found in the independent review: the project's own test commands got the safe git environment (no local clones, empty hooks path), which could show up as false TEST_FAILURE findings. They run the project's code anyway and now keep the normal environment
Found in the independent review: $ in a path was expanded by systemd in ExecStart; it is now written as $$

Driver keys are listed from the engine's working folder, not the scanned project; for an engine whose working folder is its output folder (CodeQL, only with --run-tests) the project's drivers are not listed
Semgrep is installed in CI by exact version, not with --require-hashes, and its dependencies are resolved by pip; trivy and gitleaks are SHA-256 checked

First real ZAP run on Windows crashed: zap.sh was picked from PATH and CreateProcess cannot start a shell script; an OSError became a traceback. ZAP now runs as java -jar from PATH or the tools folder, and a start failure is a clear note
findings.check: tests/test_v7_pentest.py::test_find_zap_uses_java_jar_from_the_tools_folder_not_a_shell_script, test_zap_that_cannot_start_is_a_note_not_a_traceback; real ZAP 2.17.0 run on 2026-11-03 found 9 alerts on a throwaway local site

findings.where: scripts/agent_guard.py file_cmd (grep, egrep, fgrep, rg, ag, ack), scan(), awk()
findings.what: From the outside product review and a live false positive: option names were folded to lower case, so grep -E/-F/-A/-C were read as -e/-f (pattern or pattern file) and the next word was taken as their value. A quoted pattern was then judged as a path (false positive), and a real path after the pattern was skipped (grep -E 'a|b' ~/.claude/settings.json was allowed in managed mode, a bypass of the outside-the-project check). awk regex literals like /a|b/ were read as a pipe to a command. Options are now case sensitive per tool, short clusters (-nE, -A3, -nf FILE) follow getopt, rg --hostname-bin is unmodelled like --pre, and awk regex and string contents are blanked before the pipe and redirect check

Gemini CLI and Antigravity had the rules and the gate but no agent guard. Both now have an adapter checked against the official hook docs: Gemini CLI BeforeTool (exit 0 or 2 only, because other exits and non-JSON output fail open there; ask becomes deny), Antigravity PreToolUse (allow, deny, force_ask; an explicit JSON decision on every path). Malformed input fails closed. Antigravity's behaviour when the hook itself crashes or times out is not documented and is untested

findings.where: ONE_PROMPT_INSTALL.md, README.md (Install with one prompt, Install by hand)
findings.what: Two install routes disagreed: ONE_PROMPT_INSTALL.md installed from a fixed local folder and installed scanners with winget and pip, while the README said the agent installs pinned, hash-checked scanners. Both now name one route: download zip and .sig, check the key fingerprint published in SECURITY.md on main (the trust anchor), verify with ssh-keygen, extract, install, securecode.py doctor and setup --yes after one yes, verify-global, restart

findings.where: AGENTS.md, global-CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/security-review/SKILL.md, docs/SOURCE-CODE-REVIEW.md, MANIFEST.txt, scripts/secgate.py banner and SARIF driver
findings.what: User-facing docs and the gate still said V6.2 or V6 in 7.0. They now carry the current version, and the gate banner and SARIF driver read it from GATE_VERSION

findings.where: scripts/engines/__init__.py run_engines, scripts/engines/_base.py setup_command, scripts/securecode.py doctor
findings.what: The gate's 'not run' note said 'install with securecode setup', which is not a command anyone can type from a project folder. It now prints the full installed path command for the platform, the same text as the README

Local DAST needed ZAP installed by hand. securecode setup --engine zap now installs the official ZAP 2.17.0 cross-platform zip (SHA-256 and size pinned) into <tools>/zap/ZAP_2.17.0, where local_dast finds it; doctor shows it; Java 17+ is checked with java -version and reported, never installed. local_dast now uses the same tools folder rule as setup (XDG_DATA_HOME was ignored before)
The test skipped on Linux ('junctions are Windows only') and failed the new skip check. It now uses a symlink on Linux and macOS and a junction on Windows, so the same protection is tested everywhere
findings.check: tests/test_v7_rules.py::test_linked_app_folder_is_not_walked (run under Linux via WSL with a real symlink on 2026-11-03: HIGH as expected)

findings.where: scripts/agent_guard.py awk(), awk_code_only(), grep/rg/ag/ack option tables, opt_lookup_exact
findings.what: Found in the independent review of the first S2 fix (before it shipped): a regex holding a quote read as a division hid system(), getline, ENVIRON and redirects behind a fake string; gawk @f() indirect calls, -i/-E/--exec/--file=/-l, -i inplace and ARGV/ARGC were not modelled; GNU-style prefix matching resolved grep --binary to --binary-files and skipped the real file; --reg=x was not seen as an explicit pattern; ag and ack reused rg's table where -r, -t and -f are flags; ag -p reads a file; rg --files took the folder as a pattern; ag --pager and ack --output run code. Keywords are now checked on the raw awk program, only -F and -v are modelled, regex versus division follows awk's grammar and fails closed when unclear, # comments are dropped, option lookup is exact with abbreviations of value options unmodelled, and ag and ack have their own tables

Found in the independent review: dir_path (Gemini) and Cwd (Antigravity) became the event cwd, which the guard trusts as a project root, so rm -rf or a hosts file edit in any folder was allowed. The folder change is now an explicit cd the guard judges. Also fixed: read_many_files ignored paths when include was set; broad globs with default excludes off; the legacy path key of grep_search, search_file_content and glob; unknown Gemini tools kept their raw name (now mcp__gemini__<name>, so outside paths are the unknown class); save_memory now needs approval; Antigravity grep_search Includes and send_command_input Input are judged; a failed answer write in the Gemini adapter is exit 2, never the fail-open exit 1

Ahead of the output secret shield and MCP manifest lock: .security/shield-audit.jsonl and .security/mcp-lock.json are protected like guard-audit.jsonl (no write, truncate, move or delete through shell, Write, Edit or MCP, in either mode; reads allowed), and removing or moving the whole .security folder is refused, so the agent cannot erase the audit or approve a changed MCP tool by editing the lock. Writing other files inside .security stays allowed

git clean -fdx and find . -delete style commands that remove the whole tree can still remove .security with its audit files; only direct rm, rmdir, mv and Remove-Item of the folder are refused. The size cap during the ZAP download is the global 400 MB, not the pinned size (the SHA-256 check still refuses anything else)

A secret that arrived through allowed tool output (cat of a config file, a test log, an env dump, an MCP answer) reached the model; the guard only blocks reads of secret files. The shield now replaces secret values in the output (updatedToolOutput) and blocks with a reason that names the source and type
Secrets that already leaked into Claude Code transcripts and project logs could not be found without reading them by hand. The read-only sweep lists them masked, with revocation steps

MCP server configs were only noted as present (REPO_MCP_SERVERS); unpinned packages, pipe-to-shell launches, plain http, root folder access and inline secrets were not flagged. secgate full and ci now run the offline config scan on project configs

No check of the tool descriptions an MCP server serves (poisoning, hidden Unicode, shadowing) and no way to notice a server that changes its tools after approval (rug pull). Connect mode scans them and pins SHA-256 hashes in .security/mcp-lock.json

The hooks docs say telemetry captures the original output before a PostToolUse hook runs and do not say whether the transcript keeps the original or the replaced output, so a withheld secret may still sit in ~/.claude/projects. Mitigation: the sweep. Needs a live check on a real session
findings.check: manual: run a session that reads a fake secret, then py -I scripts/secret_shield.py sweep

findings.what: The agent guard does not protect .security/shield-audit.jsonl and .security/mcp-lock.json the way it protects guard-audit.jsonl, so the agent can rewrite them (re-pin a server or erase the audit). Fix belongs in agent_guard.py on the v7 branch
findings.check: tests/test_guard_positive_model.py deny cases for .security/shield-audit.jsonl and mcp-lock.json (fixed in 80a49a3)

findings.what: Not covered: output of the Monitor tool (notifications, not a tool result), secrets in the tool input, and secrets with no recognisable shape (short passwords in oddly named fields)
findings.check: documented in docs/SECRET-SHIELD-AND-MCP.md (What it does not do)

findings.what: The owner asked for OWASP ASVS coverage and the coverage page mapped only Top 10, CWE Top 25 and API Top 10. Added one row per ASVS 5.0 chapter (V1 to V17) as guidance, not a compliance claim, plus a test that every rule id cited on the page exists
README still said the Laravel lab found 17 of 18 with one miss on purpose, while benchmark/RESULTS.md shows 18 of 18 since OPEN-01 was closed

find_zap returned docker whenever docker was on PATH, before looking for the ZAP that securecode setup --engine zap installed. With Docker Desktop installed but not started, docker run failed and the scan reported 'ZAP exited N without a report' (exit 5). A local ZAP jar now wins; docker is used only when there is no local ZAP and `docker info` (argument list, 10 s timeout, output captured) succeeds; otherwise the result is status failed with the plain note 'Docker is installed but not running; start Docker Desktop or run: py -I scripts/securecode.py setup --engine zap', no traceback. ZAP_* folders and zap-*.jar files now sort by parsed version numbers (2.17 beats 2.9), the sort part of OPEN-09 (setup itself never sorted, it installs one pinned folder)

findings.where: tests/test_guard_positive_model.py, README.md (1 of 256 everyday commands asked; under 1 in 100)
findings.what: The README claims under 1 in 100 everyday commands prompt, but the corpus test only asserted an ask rate under 5 percent, so the claim could regress fivefold with CI still green. The assertion is now under 1 percent and the test is renamed to match

In ci mode a crashing required scanner (a semgrep traceback) made the gate print only that traceback, newlines turned into '?', and 'BLOCKED (ci) ... Fix the error above', hiding every built-in finding and the other scanners' results. The gate now still prints counts and all findings, shows each scanner error as a few readable lines (first two and last two, home folder as ~, secret-looking values redacted, control characters still neutralised per line), names the fix ('<name> is installed but failed to run; reinstall it or run: <installed securecode.py> setup --engine <name>') and keeps ci failing closed with exit 3. findings.json stores the same compact error text

findings.where: scripts/securecode.py setup, scripts/release/make_release.py docstring, README.md (Check a project without the AI)
findings.what: setup --engine gitleaks with gitleaks present said 'every engine this project needs is already present'; an explicit --engine request now says '<name> is already installed'. The make_release.py docstring named 6.2.1 and RELEASE-NOTES-V6.2.md; it is now version neutral. The README now explains RESULT: BLOCKED and the exit codes (0 pass, 2 a finding at or above --fail-on, 3 ci with a required scanner missing or failed), checked against secgate.main

Live test in Gemini CLI 0.50.0 on Windows: the CLI runs hook commands through PowerShell (pwsh -Command), and the template line '"<PYTHON>" -I "..."' is a PowerShell parse error. The hook exits 1, Gemini CLI treats that as a failed hook and runs the tool (fail open), so on Windows the guard never ran and nothing was blocked. Fix: settings.hooks.windows.json with the PowerShell call operator (& "<PYTHON>" ...), docs tell Windows users to use it and to test one blocked action. Rerun live: read of fake-secret/.env, shell read of it, git push --force and a write to .security/guard-audit.jsonl were all blocked (hook exit 2, tool failed, file not created); git status and a normal write ran
findings.check: tests/test_v7_guard.py::test_gemini_template_command_really_runs_in_the_cli_shell (runs the filled-in template line through the same shell wrapper Gemini CLI uses)

findings.what: Same '"<PYTHON>" -I ...' line shape as V7L-01. Not verified live: the Codex live run was stopped before a hook fired, and Antigravity is a GUI. If either runs hook commands through PowerShell on Windows, the guard fails open there too. Codex documents a commandWindows override that could carry a Windows form
findings.check: live test still to do: one blocked action per tool on Windows, with hook log evidence
